title: The Red Stripe: Seven Days on the Făgăraș Ridge, Suru to Sâmbăta
subRegion: Munții Făgăraș, Southern Carpathians (Sibiu, Argeș and Brașov counties)

bestPeriod.window: the last week of August and the first three weeks of September — snow gone from the couloirs, storms less frequent, springs still running
bestPeriod.avoid: before mid-July (old snow in Strunga Dracului and the Călțun couloirs) and after early October (first snowfalls, refuges unusable)

accommodation.note: €120–€280 (cabana beds €15–€30; refuges free; tent nights free)

transport.note: €90–€170 (Sibiu transfers, Bâlea cable car, taxi off the mountain)

activities.note: €40–€90 (bear spray bought locally, maps, one guided day)

gatewayAirport: Sibiu (SBZ) or Bucharest (OTP, 4 h by train to Sibiu/Brașov). Local train or taxi Sibiu → Turnu Roșu, 30 km. Exit by taxi from Mănăstirea Brâncoveanu to Făgăraș or Victoria, then rail to Brașov.
summary: This is the most serious walking in the Carpathians. Seventy kilometres of granite and schist crest above 2,000 metres, with two thousand-metre cirques on both sides, a chained chimney that kills people most summers,…
hook: This is the most serious walking in the Carpathians. Seventy kilometres of granite and schist crest above 2,000 metres, with two thousand-metre cirques on both sides, a chained chimney that kills people most summers, Romania's highest summit as a side trip, and huts spaced not four hours apart but a day and a half. Several of the shelters are unstaffed tin boxes with no water and no warden. You carry the week, or you do not do the week.

snapshot.Start / End: Turnu Roșu (Sebeșu de Sus) → Sâmbăta de Sus (point-to-point, ~75 km, ~6,500 m ascent)
snapshot.Getting there: Sibiu (SBZ) or Bucharest (OTP, 4 h by train to Sibiu/Brașov). Local train or taxi Sibiu → Turnu Roșu, 30 km. Exit by taxi from Mănăstirea Brâncoveanu to Făgăraș or Victoria, then rail to Brașov.

itinerary.title: Out of the forest onto the western crest
itinerary.morning: Taxi from Sibiu to **Sebeșu de Sus** above **Turnu Roșu**, the western terminus of the ridge. Buy **bear spray in Sibiu the day before** — it is legal, sold in outdoor and hunting shops, roughly 100–350 RON (€20–€70), and **it cannot be carried on any flight**, so it is a buy-on-arrival item.
itinerary.afternoon: The red stripe climbs relentlessly through beech, then spruce, then juniper. Six to seven hours to the **Suru** shelter and **Șaua Suru** below **Vârful Suru (2,283 m)**. Water in the last forest stream — fill everything.
itinerary.evening: Camp or squeeze into the refuge. This is the least-visited end of the Făgăraș and you may have the whole western crest to yourself.

itinerary.title: The long empty crest to Negoiu
itinerary.morning: Over Vârful Budislavu and **Șaua Scărișoara**, then the grassy 2,400 m dome of **Vârful Ciortea**. In cloud this is the section where people lose the line — bearings, not instinct.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue over Șaua Gropilor and the Serbota flank, then drop north on the marked descent to **Cabana Negoiu (1,546 m)**, the historic Sibiu-side hut, for a bed, a shower and a hot meal [VERIFY: current Cabana Negoiu rates and whether it is staffed for the full 2026 season].
itinerary.evening: Eat *ciorbă de burtă* and drink one beer, not three. Tomorrow is the crux and it starts early.

itinerary.title: Negoiu, the crux, and Călțun
itinerary.morning: Leave by 06:30. Back up to the ridge and along **Custura Sărății** — narrow, airy and chained in places — to **Șaua Cleopatra**. Here the route splits.
itinerary.afternoon: **Take the Strunga Doamnei.** Reach **Vârful Negoiu (2,535 m)**, the second-highest in Romania and the finest summit on the ridge, with the Argeș cirques falling away south. Then the descent to **Lacul Călțun** and **Refugiul Călțun** at about 2,135 m — glacial tarn, boulder field, and a metal refuge with no warden and no water beyond the lake.
itinerary.evening: Filter lake water. Cook early: storms on this section reliably build from mid-afternoon and the refuge is the only shelter for hours in either direction.

itinerary.title: Over Lespezi to Bâlea Lac
itinerary.morning: The chained climb out of Călțun onto **Vârful Lespezi (2,522 m)** — steep, exposed, the second-hardest passage of the week — then Paltinu and the long crest east.
itinerary.afternoon: **Vârful Vânătoarea lui Buteanu (2,507 m)**, then down to **Șaua Capra** and **Lacul Bâlea** at 2,034 m, the glacial lake sitting at the top of the **Transfăgărășan (DN7C)**.
itinerary.evening: **Cabana Bâlea Lac** — a real bed, hot food, phone signal and, if you need to bail, the **telecabina** down to Bâlea Cascadă and the road. Note that the Transfăgărășan's restricted sector, **Bâlea Cascadă to Piscu Negru, is open only 07:00–21:00** and the road itself only opened for the 2026 season on **12 June**; it is typically shut from late October until mid-June [VERIFY: 2027 Transfăgărășan opening date].

itinerary.title: Fereastra Zmeilor and Podragu
itinerary.morning: East over **Vârful Iezerul Caprei** and Vârful Netedu on broad grassy crest — fast walking, poor navigation in cloud, and the best bear-viewing ground of the trip at dawn on the northern slopes.
itinerary.afternoon: Past **Fereastra Zmeilor**, the Dragons' Window, with its unstaffed refuge, then over Arpașu Mare and down to **Cabana Podragu (2,136 m)** beside Lacul Podragu — the highest staffed hut on the ridge and the logistical hinge of the whole traverse [VERIFY: current Podragu rates and 2026 staffing dates].
itinerary.evening: Podragu is cash-only and runs on a generator. Book by phone days ahead in August; in September you can usually walk in.

itinerary.title: Moldoveanu, 2,544 m
itinerary.morning: Leave the pack at Podragu and go light. The red stripe runs east over Vârful Podu Giurgiului and Ucea Mare to the saddle below **Vârful Viștea Mare (2,527 m)**.
itinerary.afternoon: From Viștea Mare, a fifteen-minute connecting ridge — narrow, rocky, easy in dry conditions — leads to **Vârful Moldoveanu (2,544 m)**, the **highest point in Romania**. Nine to eleven hours round trip from Podragu. Turn around at 13:00 regardless of where you are; the afternoon build here is not negotiable.
itinerary.evening: Back at Podragu, dry everything. Tomorrow is the descent and it is long.

itinerary.title: Dara, and down the Sâmbăta valley
itinerary.morning: North-east over **Vârful Dara (2,500 m)** and Vârful Hârtopu, one of the quietest and most spectacular stretches of crest, with the Podragu and Sâmbăta cirques below on either hand.
itinerary.afternoon: Down through **Fereastra Mare a Sâmbetei** into the **Valea Sâmbetei** — steep, wooded, wet underfoot — past **Cabana Valea Sâmbetei (1,401 m)** for a last meal, then out to the trailhead.
itinerary.evening: **Mănăstirea Brâncoveanu** at Sâmbăta de Sus — a Brâncovenesc-style monastery founded by Constantin Brâncoveanu, with a guesthouse and, more to the point, a road. Taxi to Victoria or Făgăraș, then rail to Brașov or Sibiu.

accommodationStrategy.name: Cabana Podragu
accommodationStrategy.description: the only staffed bed high enough to make Moldoveanu a day trip rather than a two-day expedition. Dormitory bunks, hot food, drying space, generator power, cash only.
accommodationStrategy.booking: by phone, direct, a week ahead in September and two to three weeks in August [VERIFY: current phone booking channel].

accommodationStrategy.name: Cabana Bâlea Lac
accommodationStrategy.description: the mid-route reset. Real showers, a shop, phone signal, cable car down, and the only point on the traverse where you can resupply, post a bag ahead, or abandon the walk with dignity.
accommodationStrategy.booking: online or by phone, 3–4 weeks ahead — it fills with Transfăgărășan road tourists, not hikers.

accommodationStrategy.name: Refugiul Călțun
accommodationStrategy.description: it splits the hardest 25 km of the ridge into two survivable days. No warden, no booking, no water tap, no food, 10–20 places on a first-come basis.
accommodationStrategy.booking: you cannot. Carry a tent and treat the refuge as a bonus, not a plan.

logistics.connectivity: Orange and Vodafone reach much of the crest — surprisingly good on the summits, absent in every cirque. Bâlea Lac and Podragu have signal. Download offline maps before Day 1; there is no data in the Sâmbăta and Podragu valleys.
logistics.emergency: **Salvamont 0725 826 668** and **112**. Give your position as a named summit or saddle plus your waymark colour. Response time from the crest is hours. Tell someone your route and your bail-out points before you start.
logistics.weather: The Făgăraș makes its own weather. **Convective storms build from 13:00–14:00 on most summer days**, and the ridge is the highest metal-free lightning conductor for a hundred kilometres — you are the tallest thing on it. Be off exposed crest by early afternoon. Cloud can drop visibility to twenty metres in minutes, which is the real argument for the compass.
logistics.bookingWindows: Staffed cabanas 1–3 weeks ahead by phone; refuges cannot be booked at all. August weekends are the only genuine crowding. Bear spray needs no permit but must be bought in Romania.
logistics.money: The leu, roughly 5.0–5.1 RON to the euro. **Podragu, Negoiu and Valea Sâmbetei are cash-only** — carry 800–1,200 RON (€160–€240) in small notes for the week. ATMs at Sibiu, Victoria and Făgăraș only.
logistics.transportRules: A rental car needs a **rovinietă** e-vignette, category A: €3.50 for one day, €6 for ten days, €9.50 for thirty — **there is no seven-day product**. Do not park a car at Turnu Roșu and expect to reach it; this is a point-to-point walk and the finish is 90 km from the start by road.
logistics.permits: No entry fee and no permit for the Făgăraș ridge, and **wild camping on the crest is tolerated** in practice outside strictly protected reserves — pitch on grass, never in a refuge doorway, carry out everything. Fires are prohibited above the treeline. Sheepdogs at the summer *stâne* are a genuine hazard: walk round the flock, do not run, and carry a pole.

proTips: **Take the Strunga Doamnei and do not apologise for it.** The Dracului is the famous line; the Doamnei is the one that gets you to Călțun with a heavy pack and both ankles. Guides make the same choice with clients.

**Bears are the reason your food goes in a dry bag, hung, twenty metres from the tent.** Romania holds the **largest brown bear population in Europe outside Russia**, and the Făgăraș has real density on the northern slopes and in the Sâmbăta and Podragu valleys. Cook away from where you sleep, never leave rubbish at a refuge, make noise on wooded descents at dawn and dusk, and if you meet one: do not run, back away slowly, keep the spray on your hip belt where you can reach it, not inside the pack.

**Post a resupply bag to Cabana Bâlea Lac.** It is the only road-accessible point mid-traverse, and it turns a seven-day food carry into two four-day carries — worth several kilos over the hardest days.
**Do Moldoveanu from Podragu, not from the south.** The Argeș-side approaches involve a long forest road and a bivouac; from Podragu it is a single long day with a light pack and a hot meal waiting.

**Water is the limiting factor, not distance.** There is **no water on the crest itself** — you drop to Lacul Călțun, Lacul Bâlea, Lacul Podragu, or the springs 50–150 m below the ridge on the northern side. Fill at every one, and carry four litres over the dry sections.
**Learn *"Unde este apă?"*** — where is water? — and *"Cât mai e până la refugiu?"* Shepherds know both answers and are the only people you will meet for hours.

**Go in the second week of September.** Old snow is gone from the couloirs, the storm frequency drops sharply, the August refuge scrum is over, the springs are still running, and the light on the northern cirques is the best of the year.

raw.The chain of huts and refuges — and the: Staffed and bookable: **Cabana Bâlea Lac** (2,034 m, staffed year-round, own phone/site booking, reached by road and cable car), **Cabana Bâlea Cascadă** (1,234 m, road-served), **Cabana Negoiu** (1,546 m, staffed, phone booking), **Cabana Podragu** (2,136 m, staffed in summer only, phone booking, generator power, cash), **Cabana Valea Sâmbetei** (1,401 m, staffed, phone). **Unstaffed, unbookable, first-come, no water on site, no warden, no food, no rescue on hand: Refugiul Călțun** (by Lacul Călțun, ~2,135 m), **Refugiul Fereastra Zmeilor**, and the **Suru** shelter — the original **Cabana Suru** burned down in 2003 and what stands is a small emergency refuge, not a hut [VERIFY: current status and capacity of the Suru refuge]. Refuges hold roughly 10–20 people and fill on August weekends. **Plan for a tent.** [VERIFY: current 2026 bed rates at Bâlea Lac, Negoiu, Podragu and Valea Sâmbetei]
raw.Waymarking: The main ridge is the **bandă roșie** — a red horizontal stripe between two white bands — running the full traverse from Turnu Roșu to Plaiul Foii. Descents to the north (Transylvanian) side use **blue stripe**, **red triangle** and **yellow stripe** according to valley. Be blunt about the quality: **above 2,000 m the paint is patchy, the cairns are inconsistent, and in cloud on the broad grassy summits — Ciortea, Iezerul Caprei, Podragu — the line is genuinely hard to hold.** Carry a paper map (Muntii Nostri or Dimap Făgăraș), a compass, and the GPX on two devices.
raw.Daily ascent and descent: Day 1 +1,650/−100 m. Day 2 +1,150/−900 m. Day 3 +900/−800 m. Day 4 +950/−1,050 m. Day 5 +900/−800 m. Day 6 +1,000/−1,000 m (Moldoveanu out-and-back). Day 7 +450/−1,900 m. Roughly **6,500 m of climbing** in seven days with a full pack.
raw.Strunga Dracului versus Strunga Doamnei: The classic line onto **Vârful Negoiu (2,535 m)** from Șaua Cleopatra goes through the **Strunga Dracului**, the Devil's Gully: a steep chained chimney, exposed, polished, holding old snow into July, funnelling every stone dislodged above you onto the party below. It has a fatality record. The **Strunga Doamnei** is the marked alternative on the northern side — longer, still chained in places, but far less exposed and far less prone to rockfall. **With a seven-day pack on your back, take the Strunga Doamnei.** Reserve the Dracului for a dry day, light, early, with a helmet, and only if the party is genuinely comfortable on unprotected scrambling.
raw.Gear for 2,500 m without huts: Tent or bivi bag and a bag rated to **−5 °C comfort** (September nights on the crest go below freezing). B-rated boots, helmet for the Negoiu and Călțun sections, 40 m of nothing — this is not a roped route, but gloves for the chains are essential. **4 litres of water capacity** and a filter. Full hardshell, warm layer, hat and gloves in every month. Stove and four days of food minimum, because there is no resupply between Bâlea and Sâmbăta. Headtorch, spare batteries, powerbank, and a whistle.
raw.Rescue and insurance: **Salvamont national dispatch: 0725 826 668**, plus **112**. Install the *Salvamont* and *DSU* apps, which transmit GPS. Salvamont teams operate county by county — Sibiu, Argeș and Brașov all cover parts of this ridge, and response from the crest is measured in hours, not minutes. Carry EHIC plus a policy with mountain-rescue and helicopter cover.
